source: OpenStax Psychology 2e, Chapter 8: Memory (Review Questions & Traps)

questions.question: ________ is a memory store with a phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, episodic buffer, and a central executive.
The storage capacity of long-term memory is ________.
choices: one or two bits of information
seven bits, plus or minus two

questions.question: The three functions of memory are ________.
choices: automatic processing, effortful processing, and storage
automatic processing, effortful processing, and retrieval

questions.section: 8.2 Parts of the Brain Involved with Memory
questions.question: This physical trace of memory is known as the ________.

questions.section: 8.2 Parts of the Brain Involved with Memory
questions.question: An exceptionally clear recollection of an important event is a (an) ________.
________ is when our recollections of the past are done in a self-enhancing manner.
Tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is also known as ________.
The formulation of new memories is sometimes called ________, and the process of bringing up old memories is called ________.

When you are learning how to play the piano, the statement 'Every good boy does fine' can help you remember the notes E, G, B, D, and F for the lines of the treble clef. This is an example of a (an) ________.
According to a study by Yogo and Fujihara (2008), if you want to improve your short-term memory, you should spend time writing about ________.
The self-referencing effect refers to ________.
choices: making the material you are trying to memorize personally meaningful to you
making a phrase of all the first letters of the words you are trying to memorize
making a word formed by the first letter of each of the words you are trying to memorize
saying words you want to remember out loud to yourself
questions.correct_answer: making the material you are trying to memorize personally meaningful to you

questions.question: Memory aids that help organize information for encoding are ________.

questions.section: 8.2 Parts of the Brain Involved with Memory
questions.question: What specific concentration of potassium chloride in millimoles per liter triggers long-term depression in Purkinje cells according to Chapter 8?
questions.trap_rationale: Chapter 8 discusses the cerebellum in procedural memory, but gives no ionic concentrations for Purkinje cell depression.

questions.question: According to Chapter 8, which specific year did W. Ross Ashby publish his ultrastability equations for memory networks?
questions.trap_rationale: W. Ross Ashby and ultrastability equations are not discussed or cited anywhere in Chapter 8.

questions.question: What did the 2024 fMRI study by Zhang et al. conclude about TikTok usage and episodic memory retention in adolescents according to Chapter 8?
questions.trap_rationale: OpenStax Psychology 2e was published in 2020 and mentions no 2024 studies or social media video platform effects.

questions.section: 8.2 Parts of the Brain Involved with Memory
questions.question: How many distinct histological layers of the neocortex are identified in Section 8.2 as participating in prospective memory consolidation?
questions.trap_rationale: Section 8.2 discusses gross brain areas (amygdala, hippocampus, cerebellum, prefrontal cortex) without laminar neocortical histology.

questions.question: What is the recommended pediatric therapeutic dosage of memantine in milligrams per day specified in Chapter 8 for treating mild cognitive impairment?
questions.trap_rationale: Chapter 8 mentions Alzheimer disease conceptually but gives no pharmaceutical prescription guidelines or drug dosages.
